question: Who Owns Subway?
quick_answer: Subway is owned by Roark Capital, an Atlanta-based private equity firm, which bought the sandwich chain for about $9.6 billion in a deal that completed in 2024. Before that, Subway had been privately owned by its founding families since 1965. Roark also backs restaurant groups like Inspire Brands.
key_facts: Current owner: Roark Capital (deal closed in 2024)
Founders: Fred DeLuca and Peter Buck
Was family-owned and private before the Roark sale

body.heading: Who owns Subway now?
body.text: Subway is owned by Roark Capital, a private equity firm known for investing in restaurant and franchise brands. Roark agreed to buy Subway in 2023 and completed the purchase in 2024 for about $9.6 billion. That ended decades of ownership by Subway's founding families.

body.heading: Who owned it before
body.text: Subway was founded in 1965 in Bridgeport, Connecticut, by Fred DeLuca and Peter Buck. For most of its history it stayed privately owned by those families rather than going public. The 2024 sale to Roark was the first time the company changed hands to an outside owner on this scale.

body.heading: What Roark ownership means
body.text: Roark Capital owns or backs several large restaurant names, including the Inspire Brands group. For Subway, the new ownership is aimed at funding investment and growth. Day-to-day, most Subway restaurants are still run by independent franchisees around the world.
